description: Discovery-phase backend readiness model. For a target backend, lists what the port actually needs, how to probe it on the host, the fallback when it is absent, and the impact x likelihood weight used for the Pareto ranking. Values are requirements of the backend, not claims about a specific machine: the probe decides PASS/FAIL, and an unprobed row is UNVALIDATED, never assumed. A row may carry `host_os` or `host_arch` (x86 / arm / gpu) to say where it applies: on any other host it is NOT RUN (not applicable), never FAIL, so one model covers Windows, Linux and macOS instead of three files. The `safeguards` list is backend-agnostic: it is appended to every backend's rows as advisory checks (they cannot be answered before code exists) and is evaluated for real by `postport_recheck`. They encode lessons that cost a port its performance: per-dispatch overhead, dispatch count, fusion legality, workgroup limits, utilisation, source parity, and available-vs-used extensions.

scoring.impact: 1-5. How much a miss hurts: 5 = port cannot ship, 1 = cosmetic.
scoring.likelihood: 0-1. How often this bites on a real port of this kind.
scoring.score: impact * likelihood. Pareto ranks by score; the vital few are the rows that reach 80% of the total.

evidence_labels.FAIL: probed and absent; use the fallback or stop
evidence_labels.NOT RUN: requires a build or a manual step
evidence_labels.UNVALIDATED: could not be probed; treat as absent until proven

rebar.benefit: host-mapped weight and KV streaming without a staging copy; one less full-size buffer per tensor
rebar.fallback: page-locked staging ring + chunked hipMemcpyAsync, double-buffered; keep hot tensors resident in device memory

requirements.need: hipcc that accepts the target gfx
requirements.fallback: build the hsaco on a Linux ROCm host and ship the code object; never hand-encode ISA

requirements.need: agent enumeration to confirm the target gfx is present
requirements.fallback: read the PCI id and map it to gfx manually, then record it

requirements.need: disassemble the produced hsaco to verify what was emitted
requirements.fallback: use llvm-objdump from the LLVM install; a build that cannot be inspected is not verified

requirements.need: 4-way int8 dot for quantised kernels
requirements.fallback: raw v_dot4_i32_i8 may have no gfx12 encoding; use amd_mixed_dot, else scalar expand

requirements.need: a matrix path (MFMA on CDNA, WMMA on RDNA3+)
requirements.fallback: DP4a or scalar FMA reconstruction; a matrix kernel restructured is a design change, not a flag

requirements.need: wave size known before touching shuffle/lane logic
requirements.fallback: rewrite warp intrinsics for the target width; do not pass a wave-size flag and assume it applied

requirements.need: fine-grained host-visible allocation behaviour confirmed
requirements.probe: run one host-mapped copy on target
requirements.fallback: fall back to coarse-grained + explicit copies; record which path ran

requirements.need: code object inspected: SIMD width, VGPRs, spills, LDS, exported symbols
requirements.fallback: a module that compiles but lacks the called symbol is a failure; check the symbol inventory

requirements.need: a working ROCm/HIP stack on the chosen host OS
requirements.fallback: build on Linux and ship the code object, or use the Windows ROCm build that is actually installed

rebar.benefit: larger mapped window for zero-copy weight streaming
rebar.fallback: pinned staging buffers + chunked cudaMemcpyAsync, hot tensors resident

requirements.need: nvcc for the target compute capability
requirements.fallback: match the toolkit to the driver; a newer toolkit than the driver supports produces a load failure, not a compile error

requirements.need: inspect the cubin the build produced
requirements.fallback: nvdisasm on the extracted cubin

requirements.need: tensor cores for an mma.sync port
requirements.fallback: fp32 FMA path; keep it selectable, not a silent downgrade

requirements.need: graph capture behaviour confirmed on this driver
requirements.fallback: rebuild with events; a failed capture must re-run the work, not drop it

requirements.need: managed-memory oversubscription behaviour measured
requirements.fallback: explicit device/host copies with a residency plan

requirements.need: cubin inspected: registers, spills, shared memory, symbols
requirements.fallback: assert the exported kernel list before trusting a successful build

rebar.benefit: host-visible device-local staging for large tensors without a copy
rebar.fallback: host-visible staging buffer + device-local copy, one chunk in flight per queue slot

requirements.need: GLSL to SPIR-V compiler
requirements.fallback: glslangValidator; both must target the same SPIR-V version the driver accepts

requirements.need: a working Vulkan loader and driver
requirements.fallback: install the ICD for the target vendor; a missing ICD looks like an unsupported feature

requirements.need: validate the produced SPIR-V before shipping it
requirements.fallback: let the driver report; a driver error names no line, so keep the module small

requirements.need: VK_KHR_cooperative_matrix usable for matmul (tensor path)
requirements.fallback: DP4a-style SPIR-V (VK_KHR_shader_integer_dot_product) matmul
requirements.source: README 'CooperativeMatrix is broken on AMD Vulkan' + ARCH_MAP.json#vulkan

requirements.need: subgroup width the shader will be written against
requirements.probe: vulkaninfo subgroupSize, or the device's own report
requirements.fallback: declare SUBGROUP_SIZE at build time and assert it at load

requirements.need: timeline semaphore / fence model mapped to the source stream model
requirements.fallback: single queue with explicit barriers; slower but ordered

requirements.need: SPIR-V module validated and disassembled
requirements.fallback: treat an unvalidated module as unverified

rebar.api: D3D12_HEAP_TYPE_GPU_UPLOAD / custom heap with CPU-visible VRAM (Agility SDK), DXGI budget query
rebar.benefit: CPU-writable VRAM for large weight uploads without a staging copy
rebar.fallback: D3D12_HEAP_TYPE_UPLOAD staging + CopyBufferRegion into DEFAULT heap, chunked per fence value

requirements.need: DXC to compile HLSL to DXIL
requirements.fallback: fxc only reaches SM 5.1; compute shader model 6.x needs DXC

requirements.need: Agility SDK headers for enhanced barriers and GPU upload heaps
requirements.probe: vcpkg list | findstr directxheaders  (or check the NuGet/Agility SDK package)
requirements.fallback: target the OS inbox D3D12 version and drop the newer features explicitly

requirements.need: Windows host (D3D12 is Windows-only)
requirements.fallback: use Vulkan on non-Windows; do not emulate D3D12

requirements.need: enhanced barrier support queried, not assumed
requirements.fallback: legacy resource-state transitions; correct but more transitions

requirements.need: DXGI memory budget queried before sizing the working set
requirements.fallback: size from the modelled budget and stream the remainder

requirements.need: DXIL container inspected for the target shader model
requirements.fallback: unvalidated DXIL is unverified; check the shader model in the container

rebar.api: USM host allocations mapped into the device address space
rebar.benefit: fewer explicit copies when the BAR window covers the working set
rebar.fallback: USM device allocation + explicit memcpy, or buffer/accessor with a copy plan

requirements.need: icpx/dpcpp with the SYCL front end
requirements.fallback: the oneAPI DPC++ compiler is the same front end; a plain clang without SYCL will not compile the code

requirements.need: enumerate devices and confirm the target is visible to SYCL
requirements.fallback: query through the runtime API once and record the device string

requirements.need: USM support confirmed, since the port may rely on shared pointers
requirements.fallback: buffer/accessor model; semantics differ, so test the copy boundaries

requirements.need: subgroup size known before porting shuffles
requirements.fallback: work-group reduction

requirements.need: a matrix path on the target device
requirements.fallback: scalar or dp4a path; joint_matrix support differs per device

requirements.need: the device image inspected for the intended target
requirements.fallback: an unvalidated device image is unverified

rebar.benefit: Apple silicon uses unified memory; there is no discrete BAR window to enlarge

requirements.need: Metal compiler from the Xcode toolchain
requirements.fallback: there is no portable substitute for the Metal front end

requirements.need: macOS host (Metal is Apple-only)
requirements.fallback: another backend; Metal cannot be emulated

requirements.need: simdgroup width and matrix support known
requirements.fallback: threadgroup reduction

requirements.need: metallib inspected for the intended GPU family
requirements.fallback: an uninspected metallib is unverified

rebar.benefit: a CPU has no PCIe BAR window: system memory is directly addressable, so there is no large-BAR path to win or lose

requirements.need: MSVC for the Windows CRT and the target /arch flags
requirements.fallback: run inside a developer prompt (vcvars64.bat) or use clang-cl with the same CRT; the SIMD flags differ between them

requirements.need: a C/C++ compiler that takes the target -m flags
requirements.fallback: clang takes the same vector extensions for the common intrinsics; check the builtin spellings you rely on

requirements.need: clang, which is the only portable compiler on macOS and the one that accepts the widest intrinsic set
requirements.fallback: the platform compiler; verify every `__builtin_` spelling before assuming it exists

requirements.need: one build description that survives all three hosts
requirements.fallback: a plain Makefile plus a .bat equivalent; keep the flag sets in one file, not three

requirements.need: AVX2+FMA, the baseline every x86-64 SIMD port assumes
requirements.probe: CPU ISA flags (probe) or the fed fact
requirements.fallback: restructure for the target's own width: NEON on aarch64, SSE2/AVX if AVX2 is absent, or a scalar path that is correct first

requirements.need: fused multiply-add, which the GEMM inner loop is written around
requirements.probe: CPU ISA flags (probe) or the fed fact
requirements.fallback: separate multiply and add: identical results only if the reference does not depend on the fused rounding

requirements.need: AVX-512 only if the kernels are written for 512-bit vectors
requirements.probe: CPU ISA flags (probe) or the fed fact
requirements.fallback: ship the AVX2 path. Never gate on a CPU name: consumer 12th-14th gen parts have AVX-512 fused off, which is why this row is probed and not read from a table

requirements.need: a BLAS whose precision matches what the kernels assume (oneMKL, OpenBLAS or Accelerate)
requirements.probe: link one GEMM on each OS and compare against the reference
requirements.fallback: write the GEMM; a BLAS that silently uses a different precision is an accuracy bug, not a speed choice

requirements.need: a host the port is actually built and run on
requirements.fallback: cross-build and ship the binary, or drop the OS from the support matrix explicitly

requirements.need: the produced binary inspected: ISA baseline, BLAS linkage, symbols
requirements.fallback: an uninspected binary may have been built for the build host's ISA rather than the target's

requirements.need: NEON/ASIMD for the vector path
requirements.probe: aarch64: /proc/cpuinfo Features asimd, or sysctl on macOS
requirements.fallback: portable scalar kernels (roughly 4-8x slower on the vector path)

requirements.need: SDOT/UDOT (FEAT_DotProd) for int8 quantised matmul
requirements.probe: aarch64: Features asimddp; macOS: sysctl hw.optional.arm.FEAT_DotProd
requirements.fallback: multiply-accumulate widening pair instead of SDOT

safeguards.need: the cost of ONE dispatch on this target, measured, because it is a design parameter and not a constant: the same engine structure that is free on one driver is 92% of token time on another
safeguards.probe: time N identical dispatches with a trivial body (pipeline bound once) and divide; do not trust a traced number, tracing inflates per-dispatch cost. Compare with dispatches/iteration.
safeguards.fallback: if overhead x dispatches/iteration is more than half of iteration time, fix granularity before any kernel micro-optimisation
safeguards.source: Meteor Lake Vulkan case: ~385 us/dispatch on Intel vs ~100 us AMD, 116 GEMV dispatches/token = 92% of 48.4 ms

safeguards.need: dispatches (or kernel launches) per iteration/token, counted on the ported tree, and the same number on the source platform
safeguards.probe: count launches for exactly one iteration (trace, API hook, or a counter in the submit path)
safeguards.fallback: reduce the count: fuse stages whose dependency is per-element or per-row; never assume a redundant dispatch is cheap
safeguards.source: Meteor Lake: ~263 dispatches/token against ~1.7 ms of real compute

safeguards.need: for every stage pair you intend to fuse, the dependency shape: per-element, per-row, or cross-workgroup reduction
safeguards.probe: classify each edge by what the consumer reads: one element, one row, or ALL of the producer's output
safeguards.fallback: a cross-workgroup edge keeps its dispatch boundary or needs a device-wide barrier; on a backend without one (Vulkan compute) fusion there is not available at any workgroup size
safeguards.source: Meteor Lake truth table: gate+up silu fusable (per-row); silu->down NOT fusable (down reads all silu)

safeguards.need: the largest workgroup/subgroup configuration this target driver actually runs, verified by running it
safeguards.probe: sweep the size (64..1024) with the real shader and time each; a driver crash or slowdown is the answer, not a bug in the shader
safeguards.fallback: stay at the largest verified size; larger is not faster when the driver serialises or spills
safeguards.source: Meteor Lake: driver unstable above WG=256; the fused shader at WG=1024 was 47% slower

safeguards.need: achieved arithmetic or bandwidth as a fraction of this target's peak, computed rather than felt
safeguards.probe: measured ops/s or bytes/s for the kernel divided by the spec peak for that datatype
safeguards.fallback: below a few percent of peak the bottleneck is the driver or the dispatch model: stop tuning the inner loop
safeguards.source: Meteor Lake: 20.65 tok/s = 0.03% of peak; the GEMV itself needs ~15 us of 400

safeguards.need: target throughput against the platform the design came from, same workload and same quantisation
safeguards.probe: run the same model and quant format on both; do not compare against a paper number
safeguards.fallback: attribute the delta before changing kernels: a uniform slowdown across every kernel is a per-dispatch or per-copy cost, not one bad kernel
safeguards.source: Meteor Lake: 32-34 tok/s on AMD -> 20.65 tok/s on Intel, identical kernels

safeguards.need: for each extension/feature the plan leans on: advertised by the device, enabled at creation, and actually exercised by the shader
safeguards.probe: enumerate device extensions, then check the create-info and grep the shader/pipeline for the feature; all three must hold
safeguards.fallback: available != enabled != used != faster. If it is enabled but unused, the win is unmeasured, not proven
safeguards.source: Meteor Lake: VK_EXT_descriptor_buffer, push_descriptor, shader_object, timeline_semaphore, buffer_device_address all available; buffer_device_address enabled and unused
